projectBackground.name: AI Governance Review — Candidate Screening Tool
projectBackground.context: Orbis wants to buy an AI tool that ranks job applicants. The board asks whether it is safe and lawful to use.

manager.name: Rachel Osei
manager.note: Say what the law and ethics require, in plain words, and what evidence would satisfy a regulator.

assignment.title: Assess the screening tool
assignment.brief: Classify risk, calculate the impact ratio, define oversight and data rules and write the assessment.

documents.name: Vendor Statement
documents.note: Tool ranks CVs and auto-rejects the bottom 40%.

documents.name: Selection Data
documents.note: Group A selected 100 of 200 (50%); Group B 45 of 150 (30%).

documents.name: Data Inventory
documents.note: Tool ingests CV, photo and social media profile.

tasks.title: Risk Classification
tasks.prompt: A tool that screens job applicants is generally treated as:
tasks.reasoning: Employment decisions affect rights and livelihoods.
tasks.mistake: Treating it as low-risk skips mandatory controls.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Impact Ratio
tasks.prompt: Group A selection rate 50%; Group B selection rate 30%. What is the impact ratio B/A?
tasks.reasoning: A ratio below 0.8 signals possible adverse impact.
tasks.mistake: Ignoring the ratio ignores discrimination risk.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Human Oversight
tasks.prompt: The tool auto-rejects 40% of applicants. What control is needed?
options: Meaningful human review before final rejection
tasks.reasoning: Important decisions need real human oversight.
tasks.tip: Reviewers must be able to override.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Documentation
tasks.prompt: Select documents to require from the vendor.
options: Description of training data and its limitations
tasks.mistake: Accepting claims without evidence is risk.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Data Minimisation
tasks.prompt: The tool ingests photos and social media. What principle applies?
options: Collect only data necessary and relevant to the job
tasks.reasoning: Minimisation protects candidates and reduces risk.
tasks.mistake: Extra data creates bias and breach risk.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Assessment Summary
tasks.prompt: Write a 3-5 sentence assessment summary for the board.
tasks.modelAnswer: The screening tool is a high-risk AI system. Selection data shows an impact ratio of 0.60, below the 0.8 guideline, so we cannot recommend deployment without further investigation. Automatic rejection of 40% of applicants should be replaced by human review, and photo and social media inputs removed under data minimisation. We recommend procurement only after the vendor provides bias testing, documentation and an appeal process.
tasks.reasoning: A good assessment states risk level, evidence, conditions and the decision.
tasks.mistake: A yes without conditions is irresponsible.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

caseStudy.title: Case Study: The Recruiter That Preferred One Profile
caseStudy.background: A recruitment algorithm trained on past hires down-ranked applicants from certain backgrounds. The company withdrew it after journalists exposed the pattern.
caseStudy.challenges: Bias was never tested before launch.
caseStudy.solution: Kestrel requires pre-deployment bias tests and human review of rejections.
caseStudy.lessonsLearned: Test for bias before and after deployment.
